Smooth death rates on the grid

Source: R/harmonise-smooth.R
mt_smooth.Rd

Smooths death rates over age, over time or over both, with the exposures as weights or offset. Deaths are replaced by exposure times the smoothed rate; exposures are unchanged. Cells with missing deaths do not enter the fit and stay missing (only the 2D GAM predicts them). Deaths and exposures must be available on the grid (use mt_ungroup() first for grouped data). In a forecasting pipeline, use it as a preprocessing step (mt_prep(step_smooth(...))): models are then fitted to the smoothed rates, while their residuals, observed rates, backtest scales and jump-off offsets come from the deaths before smoothing ("smooth input, raw residuals"). Predictive draws add Poisson deaths given the model's rates, as without smoothing.

Usage

mt_smooth(
  data,
  dims = 1,
  lambda = NULL,
  criterion = c("bic", "aic"),
  kr = 2,
  deg = 3,
  pord = 2,
  lambda_range = c(0.01, 1e+08),
  method = c("pspline", "whittaker", "gam"),
  ages = NULL,
  along = c("age", "period"),
  k = NULL
)

Arguments

data

An mt_data object.

dims

1 (over one direction, see along) or 2 (age-period surface; "pspline" or "gam").

lambda

Fixed smoothing parameter(s) of the P-splines or the Whittaker smoother; NULL selects them.

criterion

"bic" or "aic".

kr

Knot spacing in years (age and period).

deg, pord

Degree of the B-splines and order of the difference penalty.

lambda_range

Search range of the smoothing parameters of the P-splines and the Whittaker smoother (in both directions).

method

"pspline" (Poisson P-splines, default), "whittaker" or "gam" (package mgcv); see Details. With dims = 1 and along = "period" the default is "whittaker".

ages

Range of ages that is smoothed, c(lower, upper); other ages keep their observed deaths and do not enter the fit. By default all ages except the first year of life when the grid starts with age 0 as its own interval (infant mortality does not follow the age pattern of the following ages).

along

For dims = 1: "age" or "period" ("whittaker" only).

k

Basis dimensions of the tensor-product smooth for dims = 2, method = "gam": ages and years (default: up to 10 each).

Value

An mt_data object with smoothed deaths; diagnostics as attribute "smooth", one row per fit, with the smoothing parameter, the effective degrees of freedom (edf, or ed for P-splines) and, for the Whittaker smoother, at_bound when the selected parameter is at an end of lambda_range before the fit reached its limit there (interpolation at the lower end, a polynomial of degree pord - 1 at the upper end); such fits are also reported with a warning.

Details

Methods and directions:

  • dims = 1, along = "age" (default): each year separately over age, with Poisson P-splines and the exposures as offset ("pspline"; the one-dimensional case of Currie, Durban and Eilers 2004), the weighted Whittaker smoother of log rates with the deaths as weights ("whittaker"; Whittaker 1923; Eilers 2003), or a quasi-Poisson additive model s(age) with the exposures as offset ("gam"; Wood 2017), smoothing parameter by REML and overdispersion estimated;

  • dims = 1, along = "period": each age separately over time, the weighted Whittaker smoother of log rates with the deaths as weights (the approximate inverse variances of the log rates);

  • dims = 2: the age-period surface, with a Poisson P-spline surface ("pspline"; Currie, Durban and Eilers 2004) or a quasi-Poisson additive model with a tensor-product P-spline te(age, year) and the exposures as offset ("gam"; Wood 2017), smoothing parameters by REML and overdispersion estimated, so that year-to-year variation beyond Poisson noise is not taken for signal.

With "pspline", an open age interval of the grid is expanded into single years up to omega and its exposure is split by the PCLM of the exposures, as in mt_ungroup() (open_split = "pclm", Rizzi, Gampe and Eilers 2015).

The Whittaker smoother minimises sum(w (y - z)^2) + lambda sum((D z)^2) for log rates y, weights w and differences D of order pord (divided differences over age, so that groups of different widths are smoothed on the age scale). Its smoothing parameter is chosen for every fit separately, by generalised cross-validation within lambda_range: for each year (over age) or for each age (over time) and stratum. Over time, with deaths as weights, ages whose year-to-year variation is large relative to their Poisson noise (typically ages with many deaths) are smoothed little or not at all, and ages with few deaths may be smoothed to a straight line of the log rates. The P-spline fits choose their smoothing parameters by criterion within lambda_range.

Where a method needs one age per cell (the Whittaker smoother over age and the GAMs), an open last interval such as 90+ is placed at its lower bound plus half the width of the interval below it (92.5 after 85-89), a convention of this package. The P-splines instead expand the open interval into single years up to omega, as mt_ungroup() does.

Smoothing over time removes year-to-year fluctuations from the fitted trends and from the starting level of forecasts; the last years are estimated from one side only. It also removes the year-to-year variation from which models such as Lee-Carter estimate the uncertainty of their period index, so their intervals become too narrow unless the spread is re-estimated against the raw observations (recalibrated()). Smoothing over age alone changes little for large populations and helps for sparse data such as cause-specific rates of small regions. Whether smoothing improves a forecast is a question for a backtest; the vignette "Smoothing death rates" shows one. Use mt_smooth_check() to see how much was removed and mt_plot_smooth() to look at it. The 2D P-spline surface is slow for many ages and years (minutes per stratum); the 2D GAM takes about a second.

References

Currie ID, Durban M, Eilers PHC (2004). Smoothing and forecasting mortality rates. Statistical Modelling 4(4): 279-298.

Eilers PHC (2003). A perfect smoother. Analytical Chemistry 75(14): 3631-3636.

Whittaker ET (1923). On a new method of graduation. Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society 41: 63-75.

Wood SN (2017). Generalized Additive Models: An Introduction with R (2nd ed.). CRC Press.

Examples

x <- mt_example(years = 2001:2003, deaths = "single")
s <- mt_smooth(x)
head(attr(s, "smooth"))
#>    measure stratum period     method lambda_age lambda_period       ed
#>     <char>   <int> <char>     <char>      <num>         <num>    <num>
#> 1:  deaths       1   2001 pspline_1d   61501.32            NA 6.073524
#> 2:  deaths       1   2002 pspline_1d   29356.92            NA 7.071097
#> 3:  deaths       1   2003 pspline_1d   23158.84            NA 7.425411
#> 4:  deaths       2   2001 pspline_1d   91819.37            NA 5.632183
#> 5:  deaths       2   2002 pspline_1d   20711.87            NA 7.711462
#> 6:  deaths       2   2003 pspline_1d   76056.64            NA 5.855391
#>    max_rel_diff at_bound open_iterations open_converged
#>           <num>   <lgcl>           <int>         <lgcl>
#> 1:    0.1938111    FALSE              NA             NA
#> 2:    0.2021510    FALSE              NA             NA
#> 3:    0.1978243    FALSE              NA             NA
#> 4:    0.2241836    FALSE              NA             NA
#> 5:    0.2471245    FALSE              NA             NA
#> 6:    0.2149863    FALSE              NA             NA
xt <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 2000:2015)
st <- mt_smooth(xt, along = "period", method = "whittaker")
mt_smooth_check(xt, st)
